title: Curated summary: Diabetes eating basics (plate method and carbs)
text:
Diabetes eating basics: carbs, regular meals, and the plate method. Curated summary of the CDC page "Diabetes Meal Planning".
Carbs: carbohydrates in food raise blood sugar. Drinking fruit juice raises blood sugar faster than eating whole fruit, and eating carbs with protein, fat, or fiber slows the rise. (Page section: "Why a meal plan is important".)
Regular meals: plan regular, balanced meals to avoid high or low blood sugar. Eating about the same amount of carbs at each meal can help. (Page section: "Why a meal plan is important".)
Plate method: start with a 9-inch dinner plate. Fill half with nonstarchy vegetables such as salad, green beans, and broccoli. Fill one quarter with a lean protein such as chicken, beans, tofu, or eggs. Fill one quarter with carb foods. Choose water or a low-calorie drink such as unsweetened iced tea. (Page section: "The plate method".)
Carb foods include grains, starchy vegetables such as potatoes and peas, rice, pasta, beans, fruit, and yogurt. A cup of milk also counts as a carb food. (Page section: "The plate method".)
A good meal plan includes more nonstarchy vegetables, fewer added sugars and refined grains such as white bread, rice, and pasta, and whole foods instead of highly processed foods. (Page section: "Why a meal plan is important".)
Ask your doctor or a registered dietitian how many carbs you should aim for at each meal. (Page section: "Counting carbs".)
